subject.title: feat: contextual group activation — LLM-driven peeking/engaged state machine

question: Should OpenClaw add LLM-driven contextual activation for group chats, and should that behavior live in shared core activation or behind a plugin/channel API seam?
rationale: Automation can prove the current gap, but cannot choose the privacy boundary, provider exposure, config contract, logging policy, or long-term ownership for processing unmentioned group traffic.

options.title: Sponsor default-off design first
options.body: Approve a maintainer-owned design covering consent, provider exposure, retention/logging, config schema, channel coverage, and tests before accepting implementation.

options.title: Narrow to ambient room paths
options.body: Improve docs or ergonomics around existing ambient room events and message-tool-only replies instead of adding a new LLM decision state machine.

options.title: Defer to plugin/API design
options.body: Pause core activation changes until a trusted observation or decision hook can safely support this as plugin-owned behavior.

recommendation.title: Sponsor default-off design first
recommendation.body: Approve a maintainer-owned design covering consent, provider exposure, retention/logging, config schema, channel coverage, and tests before accepting implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter Steinberger introduced the existing group activation surface and is the strongest history candidate for the product boundary decision.
